447:  *
448:  *   p_0 = v ;  p_next = alpha * (Q^T * p + d * v) + (1 - alpha) * v
449:  *
450:  * Initialize p to v. Stop when the L1 difference between consecutive
451:  * distributions is below `tol`, or after `maxIter` iterations; an iteration cap
452:  * is NOT proof of convergence, so `converged` must be false when the cap is
453:  * hit. Do not force any node's score to equal the restart probability.
454:  *
455:  * TRANSITION SOURCE - part of the contract you must implement:
456:  *  - `opts.transition` present (a {@link TransitionSpec}, e.g.
457:  *    `REFERENCE_GRAPH.transition`): propagate on THAT matrix and do not require
458:  *    the global `GRAPH`. `Q` is already row-normalized, so do not re-normalize
459:  *    it; read `danglingMask` by position (`danglingMask[i]` is 1 iff node `i` is
460:  *    zero-degree). This is how the HW6 harness runs your implementation on the
461:  *    4-node reference fixture.
462:  *  - `opts.transition` absent: behave exactly as for MovieLens - require the
463:  *    global `GRAPH` (from `buildGraph` + `rowNormalize`) and build the
464:  *    transition from its `R` / `degree`.
465:  *  - Neither present: throw a clear Error; never silently fall back to a
466:  *    uniform distribution.
467:  *
468:  * NODE-INDEX CONVENTION: node indices are global positions. For the MovieLens
469:  * graph they follow `buildGraph` (users `[0, nUsers)`, then movies
470:  * `[nUsers, nUsers + nMovies)`, no padding node). For a supplied
471:  * `opts.transition` they follow `Q`'s own order. `p[i]` is the probability of
472:  * node `i` in that same order.
473:  *
474:  * The zero-degree policy must be identical here and in `personalizedPageRank`.
475:  *
476:  * @param {number} alpha Link-following probability in [0, 1]; 1 - alpha restarts.
477:  * @param {{tol?: number, maxIter?: number, transition?: TransitionSpec}} [opts]
478:  *   Defaults tol = 1e-6, maxIter = 500, transition absent (use the global GRAPH).
479:  * @returns {PageRankResult} `{p, iterations, residual, converged}`: `p` is a
480:  *   Float64Array over node indices that sums to ~1; `iterations` is the number
481:  *   of updates performed; `residual` is the final L1 difference
482:  *   `sum_j |p_next[j] - p[j]|`; `converged` is true only when `residual < tol`
483:  *   before the iteration cap was reached.
484:  * @throws {Error} when neither `opts.transition` nor the global `GRAPH` exists.
485:  */
486: function pageRank(alpha, opts) {
487:   return graphStudentPropagate(null, alpha, opts);
488: }
489: 
490: /**
491:  * Personalized PageRank with a one-hot restart at one user's node.
492:  *
493:  * Identical to `pageRank` except the restart vector v is one-hot at
494:  * one node. It accepts the same `opts.transition` override, the same stopping
495:  * rule, the same zero-degree policy and the same return shape
496:  * `{p, iterations, residual, converged}`.
497:  *
498:  * RESTART INDEX (node index, not a raw user id): the first argument is a node
499:  * INDEX and is used directly as the restart node. This is today's caller
500:  * convention; keep it.
501:  *  - default MovieLens path: the index is a global node index from `buildGraph`
502:  *    (a user node is `GRAPH.nodeOfUser(userId)` or equivalently any
503:  *    `index < GRAPH.nUsers`).
504:  *  - `opts.transition` path: the index must be in `[0, Q.length)` and refers to
505:  *    the same node order as `Q` (`REFERENCE_GRAPH.transition.nodeLabels` names
506:  *    the fixture's nodes for display).
507:  *
508:  * FAILURE CASES: an unknown / out-of-range restart index must throw a clear
509:  * Error naming the index rather than silently falling back to a uniform
510:  * restart; and when neither `opts.transition` nor the global `GRAPH` is
511:  * available, throw instead of guessing.
512:  *
513:  * @param {number} userId Node index of the restart node (see RESTART INDEX).
514:  * @param {number} alpha  Link-following probability in [0, 1]; 1 - alpha restarts.
515:  * @param {{tol?: number, maxIter?: number, transition?: TransitionSpec}} [opts]
516:  *   Same options as `pageRank`; defaults tol = 1e-6, maxIter = 500, transition
517:  *   absent (use the global GRAPH).
518:  * @returns {PageRankResult} `{p, iterations, residual, converged}` (see `pageRank`).
519:  * @throws {Error} when the restart index is unknown / out of range, or when
520:  *   neither `opts.transition` nor the global `GRAPH` exists.
521:  */
522: function personalizedPageRank(userId, alpha, opts) {
523:   if (!Number.isInteger(userId) || userId < 0) {
524:     throw new Error("personalizedPageRank: invalid restart node index " + String(userId));
525:   }
526:   return graphStudentPropagate(userId, alpha, opts);
527: }
528: 
529: /**
530:  * Plain-array memoization for an immutable graph, one option tuple at a time.
531:  * Weak keys allow discarded graphs to be collected; no tensors are retained.
532:  * Matches the instructor cache's graph-identity assumption. Returned vectors
533:  * are copied so callers cannot mutate cached probabilities. At MovieLens size,
534:  * one full user population occupies about 19 MB of probability-array storage.
535:  */
536: const graphStudentPropagationCache = new WeakMap();
537: 
538: /**
539:  * Shared synchronous tensor power iteration for the two student entry points.
540:  * A null seed means uniform restart; otherwise seed is a GLOBAL NODE INDEX.
541:  * Explicit transitions are validated, never re-normalized. The MovieLens path
542:  * keeps rectangular R (CPU/WebGL), or incoming source/segment indices (WASM),
543:  * plus degree vectors, never a square Q. WASM's fused sparseSegmentSum avoids
544:  * multiplying structural zeros. Indices are derived from binary R once per
545:  * call; propagation itself stays entirely in tensor operations. Missing
546:  * segments are zero, and trailing isolated destinations are padded with zero
547:  * output rows to the EXISTING node count, never added as graph nodes.
548:  * All tensors are owned by this call and disposed even on failure. Synchronous
549:  * dataSync reads preserve the instructor adapters' non-Promise return contract.
550:  *
551:  * @param {number|null} seed Restart position, not a raw MovieLens user ID.
552:  * @param {number} alpha Link-following probability in [0, 1].
553:  * @param {Object} [opts] tol > 0; integer maxIter >= 0; optional TransitionSpec.
554:  * @returns {PageRankResult} Float64Array output (tensor arithmetic is float32).
555:  * @throws {Error} For missing/empty graphs, invalid options or transitions/seeds.
556:  */
557: function graphStudentPropagate(seed, alpha, opts) {
558:   const options = opts || {};
559:   const tol = options.tol === undefined ? 1e-6 : options.tol;
560:   const maxIter = options.maxIter === undefined ? 500 : options.maxIter;
561:   if (!Number.isFinite(alpha) || alpha < 0 || alpha > 1 ||
562:       !Number.isFinite(tol) || tol <= 0 || !Number.isInteger(maxIter) || maxIter < 0) {
563:     throw new Error("PageRank: require alpha in [0, 1], tol > 0 and integer maxIter >= 0.");
564:   }
565:   const explicit = options.transition !== undefined;
566:   const transition = options.transition;
567:   const graph = explicit ? null : getGraph();
568:   if (!explicit && !graph) throw new Error("PageRank: no active graph or explicit transition.");
569:   if (explicit && (!transition || !Array.isArray(transition.Q))) {
570:     throw new Error("PageRank: explicit transition must contain a square Q.");
571:   }
572:   const n = explicit ? transition.Q.length : graph.nodeCount;
573:   if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n <= 0) throw new Error("PageRank: cannot propagate on an empty graph.");
574:   if (seed !== null && (!Number.isInteger(seed) || seed < 0 || seed >= n)) {
575:     throw new Error("personalizedPageRank: invalid restart node index " + String(seed) + " for " + n + " nodes.");
576:   }
577:   const mask = explicit ? transition.danglingMask : Array.from(graph.degree, d => d === 0);
578:   if (!mask || mask.length !== n) throw new Error("PageRank: dangling mask length mismatch.");
579:   if (explicit) {
580:     for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
581:       const row = transition.Q[i];
582:       if (!row || row.length !== n) throw new Error("PageRank: Q must be square.");
583:       let sum = 0;
584:       for (const value of row) {
585:         if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) throw new Error("PageRank: Q entries must be finite and nonnegative.");
586:         sum += value;
587:       }
588:       if (Math.abs(sum - (mask[i] ? 0 : 1)) > 1e-6) {
589:         throw new Error("PageRank: Q row " + i + " disagrees with its normalization/dangling mask.");
590:       }
591:     }
592:   }
593:   if (typeof tf === "undefined") throw new Error("PageRank: TensorFlow.js is unavailable.");
594:   const sparse = !explicit && tf.getBackend() === "wasm";
595:   let cache = null;
596:   if (sparse) {
597:     const key = JSON.stringify([tf.getBackend(), alpha, tol, maxIter]);
598:     cache = graphStudentPropagationCache.get(graph);
599:     if (!cache || cache.key !== key) {
600:       cache = { key, results: new Map() };
601:       graphStudentPropagationCache.set(graph, cache);
602:     }
603:     const saved = cache.results.get(seed);
604:     if (saved) return { ...saved, p: saved.p.slice() };
605:   }
606:   const restart = new Float32Array(n);
607:   if (seed === null) restart.fill(1 / n);
608:   else restart[seed] = 1;
609:   let tensors = null;
610:   let p = null;
611:   let iterations = 0;
612:   let residual = Infinity;
613:   try {
614:     tensors = tf.tidy(() => {
615:       const shared = {
616:         v: tf.tensor2d(restart, [n, 1]),
617:         mask: tf.tensor2d(Float32Array.from(mask, x => x ? 1 : 0), [n, 1]),
618:       };
619:       if (explicit) return { ...shared, Q: tf.tensor2d(transition.Q, [n, n]) };
620:       const inverse = Array.from(graph.degree, d => d > 0 ? 1 / d : 0);
621:       if (sparse) {
622:         const sources = [];
623:         const destinations = [];
624:         // Sorted destination segments represent BOTH off-diagonal blocks.
625:         // This is graph preprocessing, not a JavaScript propagation loop.
626:         for (let destination = 0; destination < n; destination++) {
627:           if (destination < graph.nUsers) {
628:             for (let i = 0; i < graph.nMovies; i++) {
629:               if (graph.R[destination][i]) {
630:                 sources.push(graph.nUsers + i);
631:                 destinations.push(destination);
632:               }
633:             }
634:           } else {
635:             const i = destination - graph.nUsers;
636:             for (let u = 0; u < graph.nUsers; u++) {
637:               if (graph.R[u][i]) {
638:                 sources.push(u);
639:                 destinations.push(destination);
640:               }
641:             }
642:           }
643:         }
644:         return { ...shared, inverse: tf.tensor2d(inverse, [n, 1]),
645:           sources: tf.tensor1d(sources, "int32"),
646:           destinations: tf.tensor1d(destinations, "int32"),
647:           segmentCount: destinations.length ? destinations[destinations.length - 1] + 1 : 0 };
648:       }
649:       return {
650:         ...shared,
651:         R: tf.tensor2d(graph.R, [graph.nUsers, graph.nMovies]),
652:         invU: tf.tensor2d(inverse.slice(0, graph.nUsers), [graph.nUsers, 1]),
653:         invM: tf.tensor2d(inverse.slice(graph.nUsers), [graph.nMovies, 1]),
654:       };
655:     });
656:     p = tensors.v.clone();
657:     while (iterations < maxIter) {
658:       const step = tf.tidy(() => {
659:         let incoming;
660:         if (explicit) {
661:           incoming = tf.matMul(tensors.Q, p, true, false);
662:         } else if (sparse) {
663:           incoming = tensors.segmentCount === 0 ? tf.zerosLike(p) : tf.pad(
664:             tf.sparse.sparseSegmentSum(p.mul(tensors.inverse), tensors.sources, tensors.destinations),
665:             [[0, n - tensors.segmentCount], [0, 0]],
666:           );
667:         } else {
668:           const pu = p.slice([0, 0], [graph.nUsers, 1]).mul(tensors.invU);
669:           const pm = p.slice([graph.nUsers, 0], [graph.nMovies, 1]).mul(tensors.invM);
670:           incoming = tf.concat([
671:             tf.matMul(tensors.R, pm),
672:             tf.matMul(tensors.R, pu, true, false),
673:           ], 0);
674:         }
675:         const dangling = p.mul(tensors.mask).sum();
676:         const next = incoming.add(tensors.v.mul(dangling)).mul(alpha)
677:           .add(tensors.v.mul(1 - alpha));
678:         const delta = next.sub(p).abs().sum().dataSync()[0];
679:         return { next, delta };
680:       });
681:       p.dispose();
682:       p = step.next;
683:       residual = step.delta;
684:       iterations++;
685:       if (!Number.isFinite(residual)) throw new Error("PageRank: non-finite propagation residual.");
686:       if (residual < tol) break;
687:     }
688:     // The original contract conservatively requires tolerance BEFORE the cap.
689:     const result = { p: Float64Array.from(p.dataSync()), iterations, residual,
690:       converged: residual < tol && iterations < maxIter };
691:     if (cache) cache.results.set(seed, { ...result, p: result.p.slice() });
692:     return result;
693:   } finally {
694:     if (p) p.dispose();
695:     if (tensors) tf.dispose(tensors);
696:   }
697: }

550: /**
551:  * Build every training-split lookup used by the provided runners and by
552:  * `recommendTopK` / `recallAtK`.
553:  *
554:  * Indexing assumptions (readme section 3.1 and 5):
555:  *   - The candidate pool is every movie observed in the training split, sorted
556:  *     ascending by raw movie id. A zero in `R` means "no positive training
557:  *     edge", never a negative preference.
558:  *   - Popularity counts distinct users whose training rating for the movie is
559:  *     `>= 4.0`; a repeated (user, movie) pair is counted once.
560:  *   - `pairsBySplit` stores the raw rated-movie sets so the exclusion rules can
561:  *     ignore the rating value ("rated in training or validation regardless of
562:  *     the rating value").
563:  *
564:  * @param {{train: Rating[], val: Rating[], test: Rating[]}} split
565:  * @returns {void}
566:  */
567: function hw6BuildSplitIndices(split) {
568:   const names = ["train", "val", "test"];
569:   const movieIds = new Set();
570:   const userIds = new Set();
571:   const positiveUsersPerMovie = new Map();
572:   const positiveUsers = new Set();
573:   let positivePairs = 0;
574: 
575:   for (let s = 0; s < names.length; s++) {
576:     const name = names[s];
577:     const list = split[name] || [];
578:     for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
579:       const row = list[i];
580:       const pairs = HW6_STATE.pairsBySplit[name];
581:       const grades = HW6_STATE.gradesBySplit[name];
582:       let pairSet = pairs.get(row.userId);
583:       if (!pairSet) {
584:         pairSet = new Set();
585:         pairs.set(row.userId, pairSet);
586:       }
587:       pairSet.add(row.movieId);
588:       let gradeMap = grades.get(row.userId);
589:       if (!gradeMap) {
590:         gradeMap = new Map();
591:         grades.set(row.userId, gradeMap);
592:       }
593:       gradeMap.set(row.movieId, row.rating);
594:     }
595:   }

597:   const train = split.train || [];

600:     movieIds.add(row.movieId);

774: /**
775:  * Deterministic 32-bit PRNG (mulberry32). Returns a function producing values
776:  * in `[0, 1)`.
777:  *
778:  * @param {number} seed
779:  * @returns {() => number}
780:  */
781: function hw6Mulberry32(seed) {
782:   let a = seed >>> 0;
783:   return function () {
784:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
785:     let t = a;
786:     t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
787:     t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
788:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
789:   };
790: }

799:   try {

801:     if (HW6_MF_MODEL.itemFactors) HW6_MF_MODEL.itemFactors.dispose();

808: /**
809:  * Batched training RMSE for a split, using the provided MF variables.
810:  *
811:  * @param {Rating[]} split
812:  * @returns {number} RMSE, or `NaN` when the model is unavailable.
813:  */
814: function hw6MfRmse(split) {
815:   if (!HW6_MF_MODEL || !split || split.length === 0) return Number.NaN;
816:   const model = HW6_MF_MODEL;
817:   return tf.tidy(function () {
818:     const n = split.length;
819:     const uRows = model.userFactors.shape[0];
820:     const iRows = model.itemFactors.shape[0];
821:     const userIds = new Int32Array(n);
822:     const movieIds = new Int32Array(n);
823:     const actual = new Float32Array(n);
824:     for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
825:       const row = split[k];
826:       userIds[k] = Math.min(Math.max(0, row.userId), uRows - 1);
827:       movieIds[k] = Math.min(Math.max(0, row.movieId), iRows - 1);
828:       actual[k] = row.rating;
829:     }
830:     const u = tf.gather(model.userFactors, tf.tensor1d(userIds, "int32"));
831:     const i = tf.gather(model.itemFactors, tf.tensor1d(movieIds, "int32"));
832:     const pred = tf.sum(tf.mul(u, i), 1).add(model.globalMean);
833:     const diff = pred.sub(tf.tensor1d(actual, "float32"));
834:     return Math.sqrt(tf.mean(diff.square()).dataSync()[0]);
835:   });
836: }

838: /**
839:  * Train the provided MF reference at most once (idempotent, lazy). Nothing here
840:  * runs on page load: the first caller that actually needs MF scores triggers it,
841:  * and every later caller reuses the cached model.
842:  *
843:  * The training pass is asynchronous and `await`s the next animation frame after
844:  * every epoch, so the page keeps painting and the `#status` line can report
845:  * progress instead of freezing for minutes. Concurrent callers share one
846:  * in-flight promise, so a second need never starts a second training run.
847:  *
848:  * Deterministic; leaves the best-validation variables in place. `MF_INFO.trainedAt`
849:  * is set only on success, and `checkpoint` stays `null` while untrained.

852:  *   the TensorFlow.js runtime is not ready, or when training throws.

854: function hw6EnsureMf() {

856:   if (HW6_MF_MODEL && MF_INFO.trainedAt !== null) return Promise.resolve(HW6_MF_MODEL);
857:   if (typeof tf === "undefined" || !HW6_STATE.splitReady) return Promise.resolve(null);

861:   HW6_MF_TRAINING = hw6TrainMf(train).then(

865:     },
866:     function (error) {

868:       console.error("MF reference training failed:", error);

870:       hw6DisposeMf();
871:       MF_INFO.checkpoint = null;
872:       MF_INFO.validationRMSE = null;

880: /**
881:  * The actual MF training loop used by `hw6EnsureMf`. Kept separate so the
882:  * in-flight promise is installed before the first `await`, which is what makes
883:  * concurrent first-needs share a single run.
884:  *
885:  * Uses `tf.tidy` per batch, disposes the scalar loss returned by
886:  * `optimizer.minimize`, and never puts an async callback inside `tf.tidy`.
887:  *
888:  * @param {Rating[]} train Training rows.
889:  * @returns {Promise<MfModel|null>}
890:  */
891: async function hw6TrainMf(train) {
892:   hw6DisposeMf();
893:   const F = MF_FACTORS;
894:   const userRows = Math.max(1, numUsers + 1);
895:   const itemRows = Math.max(1, HW6_MAX_MOVIE_ID + 1);
896:   const rand = hw6Mulberry32(MF_SEED);
897:   const normal = function () {
898:     const u = Math.max(rand(), 1e-12);
899:     const v = rand();
900:     return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v);
901:   };
902: 
903:   const uData = new Float32Array(userRows * F);
904:   for (let k = 0; k < uData.length; k++) uData[k] = normal() * 0.05;
905:   const iData = new Float32Array(itemRows * F);
906:   for (let k = 0; k < iData.length; k++) iData[k] = normal() * 0.05;
907: 
908:   let globalMean = 0;
909:   for (let i = 0; i < train.length; i++) globalMean += train[i].rating;
910:   globalMean /= train.length;
911: 
912:   const userFactors = tf.variable(tf.tensor2d(uData, [userRows, F]));
913:   const itemFactors = tf.variable(tf.tensor2d(iData, [itemRows, F]));
914:   HW6_MF_MODEL = { userFactors: userFactors, itemFactors: itemFactors, globalMean: globalMean };
915: 
916:   const optimizer = tf.train.adam(MF_CONFIG.lr);
917:   const order = new Int32Array(train.length);
918:   for (let i = 0; i < order.length; i++) order[i] = i;
919: 
920:   let bestVal = Infinity;
921:   let bestEpoch = 0;
922:   let bestU = null;
923:   let bestI = null;
924:   MF_INFO.history = [];
925: 
926:   try {
927:     for (let epoch = 1; epoch <= MF_CONFIG.epochs; epoch++) {
928:       for (let i = order.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
929:         const j = Math.floor(rand() * (i + 1));
930:         const tmp = order[i];
931:         order[i] = order[j];
932:         order[j] = tmp;
933:       }
934:       for (let start = 0; start < order.length; start += MF_CONFIG.batchSize) {
935:         const end = Math.min(start + MF_CONFIG.batchSize, order.length);
936:         const size = end - start;
937:         const uIdx = new Int32Array(size);
938:         const iIdx = new Int32Array(size);
939:         const target = new Float32Array(size);
940:         for (let k = 0; k < size; k++) {
941:           const row = train[order[start + k]];
942:           uIdx[k] = row.userId;
943:           iIdx[k] = row.movieId;
944:           target[k] = row.rating;
945:         }
946:         const cost = optimizer.minimize(
947:           function () {
948:             return tf.tidy(function () {
949:               const u = tf.gather(userFactors, tf.tensor1d(uIdx, "int32"));
950:               const it = tf.gather(itemFactors, tf.tensor1d(iIdx, "int32"));
951:               const pred = tf.sum(tf.mul(u, it), 1).add(globalMean);
952:               const mse = tf.losses.meanSquaredError(tf.tensor1d(target, "float32"), pred);
953:               const l2 = userFactors.square().sum().add(itemFactors.square().sum()).mul(MF_CONFIG.reg);
954:               return mse.add(l2);
955:             });
956:           },
957:           true,
958:           [userFactors, itemFactors],
959:         );
960:         if (cost) cost.dispose();
961:       }
962: 
963:       const trainRmse = hw6MfRmse(train);
964:       const valRmse = hw6MfRmse(HW6_SPLIT.val);
965:       MF_INFO.history.push({ epoch: epoch, trainRMSE: trainRmse, valRMSE: valRmse });
966:       if (Number.isFinite(valRmse) && valRmse < bestVal) {
967:         bestVal = valRmse;
968:         bestEpoch = epoch;
969:         bestU = userFactors.dataSync().slice();
970:         bestI = itemFactors.dataSync().slice();
971:       }
972: 
973:       // Announce progress and hand control back to the browser so the UI paints
974:       // between epochs instead of blocking the main thread.
975:       hw6SetStatus(
976:         "Training MF reference: epoch " + epoch + "/" + MF_CONFIG.epochs +
977:         " \u2014 validation RMSE " + hw6Fmt(valRmse) + "\u2026",
978:       );
979:       if (typeof tf.nextFrame === "function") {
980:         try {
981:           await tf.nextFrame();
982:         } catch (error) {
983:           // Yielding is best-effort; training still completes without it.
984:         }
985:       }
986:     }
987: 
988:     if (bestU && bestI) {
989:       tf.tidy(function () {
990:         userFactors.assign(tf.tensor2d(bestU, [userRows, F]));
991:         itemFactors.assign(tf.tensor2d(bestI, [itemRows, F]));
992:       });
993:     }
994: 
995:     MF_INFO.factors = F;
996:     MF_INFO.epochs = MF_CONFIG.epochs;
997:     MF_INFO.learningRate = MF_CONFIG.lr;
998:     MF_INFO.regularization = MF_CONFIG.reg;
999:     MF_INFO.batchSize = MF_CONFIG.batchSize;
1000:     MF_INFO.seed = MF_SEED;
1001:     MF_INFO.backend = HW6_STATE.backend;
1002:     MF_INFO.checkpoint = bestEpoch || null;
1003:     MF_INFO.validationRMSE = Number.isFinite(bestVal) ? bestVal : null;
1004:     MF_INFO.trainedAt = new Date().toISOString();
1005:     return HW6_MF_MODEL;
1006:   } catch (error) {
1007:     console.error("MF reference training failed:", error);
1008:     hw6DisposeMf();
1009:     MF_INFO.checkpoint = null;
1010:     MF_INFO.validationRMSE = null;
1011:     MF_INFO.trainedAt = null;
1012:     return null;
1013:   }
1014: }

1041: /**
1042:  * Provided MF scorer: predicted scores for the training-movie candidate pool.
1043:  *
1044:  * Scores are dot products plus the global training mean, on the same scale as
1045:  * the previous assignment's model. They are NOT comparable to PPR walk
1046:  * probabilities.

1048:  * @param {number} userId Raw user id.
1049:  * @returns {Object<number, number>} `movieId -> score`; empty when the model is
1050:  *   untrained or the user row does not exist.

1052: function mfScores(userId) {
1053:   const out = {};
1054:   const model = HW6_MF_MODEL;
1055:   if (!model) return out;
1056:   const uid = Math.round(Number(userId));
1057:   if (!Number.isFinite(uid) || uid < 0 || uid >= model.userFactors.shape[0]) return out;
1058:   const ids = HW6_STATE.candidateIds;
1059:   if (!ids.length) return out;
1060:   const F = model.userFactors.shape[1];
1061:   return tf.tidy(function () {
1062:     const idx = tf.tensor1d(Int32Array.from(ids), "int32");
1063:     const items = tf.gather(model.itemFactors, idx);
1064:     const userRow = model.userFactors.slice([uid, 0], [1, F]);
1065:     const dot = tf.matMul(items, userRow, false, true).squeeze();
1066:     const values = dot.add(model.globalMean).dataSync();
1067:     const result = {};
1068:     for (let i = 0; i < ids.length; i++) result[ids[i]] = values[i];
1069:     return result;
1070:   });

display.text:
"""Local Chrome/CDP runner for experiment.js (Python 3 + websockets).

python3 run_experiment.py start
python3 run_experiment.py eval 'HW6_EXPERIMENT.setup()' --out evidence/setup.json
Only a separate, temporary Chrome profile is controlled. Stage outputs are
saved in the project; browser/CDP settings and logs remain under /tmp/opencode.
"""
import argparse
import functools
import http.server
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
TEMP = Path('/tmp/opencode')
PORT = 8766
DEBUG = 9333


def targets():
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f'http://127.0.0.1:{DEBUG}/json', timeout=5) as response:
        return json.load(response)


def evaluate(expression):
    from websockets.sync.client import connect
    page = next(t for t in targets() if t['type'] == 'page' and f':{PORT}/' in t['url'])
    with connect(page['webSocketDebuggerUrl'], max_size=100_000_000) as ws:
        ws.send(json.dumps({'id': 1, 'method': 'Runtime.evaluate', 'params': {
            'expression': expression, 'awaitPromise': True, 'returnByValue': True}}))
        while True:
            response = json.loads(ws.recv(timeout=1200))
            if response.get('id') != 1:
                continue
            result = response.get('result', {})
            if 'error' in response or 'exceptionDetails' in result:
                raise RuntimeError(json.dumps(response, indent=2))
            return result.get('result', {}).get('value')


def reset():
    from websockets.sync.client import connect
    page = next(t for t in targets() if t['type']=='page' and f':{PORT}/' in t['url'])
    with connect(page['webSocketDebuggerUrl'], max_size=100_000_000) as ws:
        ws.send(json.dumps({'id':1,'method':'Page.reload','params':{'ignoreCache':True}}))
        while json.loads(ws.recv(timeout=30)).get('id')!=1:
            pass
    print('Reloaded the isolated experiment page. Wait for data loading, then run setup.')


class Handler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def end_headers(self):
        self.send_header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')
        super().end_headers()

def serve():
    server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', PORT), functools.partial(Handler, directory=str(ROOT)))
    chrome = subprocess.Popen([
        'google-chrome', '--headless=new', '--no-first-run', '--no-default-browser-check',
        '--disable-background-timer-throttling', '--disable-renderer-backgrounding',
        '--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows', '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader',
        f'--user-data-dir={TEMP / "hw6-chrome-profile"}', f'--remote-debugging-port={DEBUG}',
        f'http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/index.html'], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=(TEMP / 'chrome.log').open('a'))
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    finally:
        chrome.terminate()
        server.server_close()


def save(name, value):
    path = ROOT / 'evidence' / name
    temporary = path.with_suffix('.tmp')
    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
    temporary.replace(path)


def pipeline():
    """Run after setup; persist each completed stage, polling training by epoch."""
    evaluate('HW6_EXPERIMENT.backend("wasm")')
    for alpha, label in [(0.5, '050'), (0.7, '070'), (0.85, '085'), (0.95, '095')]:
        audit = evaluate(f'HW6_EXPERIMENT.validationAlpha({alpha})')
        save(f'validation-{label}.json', audit)
        save('experiment-progress.json', evaluate('HW6_EXPERIMENT.evidence'))
        print(json.dumps({'stage': 'validation', 'alpha': alpha, 'recall': audit['summary']['recall'],
                          'nonconverged': audit['summary']['nonconverged']}), flush=True)
    selection = evaluate('HW6_EXPERIMENT.selectAlpha()')
    save('selection.json', selection)
    print(json.dumps({'stage': 'selection', **selection}), flush=True)
    evaluate('''(()=>{
      window.MF_JOB={done:false,error:null};
      setTimeout(()=>{
        HW6_EXPERIMENT.trainMf('webgl').then(result=>{MF_JOB.done=true;MF_JOB.result=result;},
          error=>{MF_JOB.done=true;MF_JOB.error=String(error.stack||error);});
      },0);
      return {started:true,backend:'webgl'};
    })()''')
    last_epoch = -1
    while True:
        time.sleep(10)
        progress = evaluate('({job:MF_JOB, info:MF_INFO,status:document.getElementById("status").textContent})')
        save('mf-progress.json', progress)
        epoch = len(progress['info']['history'])
        if epoch != last_epoch:
            print(json.dumps({'stage': 'mf', 'epoch': epoch, 'status': progress['status']}), flush=True)
            last_epoch = epoch
        if progress['job']['done']:
            if progress['job']['error']:
                raise RuntimeError(progress['job']['error'])
            save('mf.json', progress['job']['result'])
            save('mf-checkpoint.json', evaluate('({info:MF_INFO,userShape:HW6_MF_MODEL.userFactors.shape,movieShape:HW6_MF_MODEL.itemFactors.shape,userFactors:Array.from(HW6_MF_MODEL.userFactors.dataSync()),movieFactors:Array.from(HW6_MF_MODEL.itemFactors.dataSync()),globalMean:HW6_MF_MODEL.globalMean})'))
            save('experiment-progress.json', evaluate('HW6_EXPERIMENT.evidence'))
            break
    result = evaluate('HW6_EXPERIMENT.testComparison()')
    save('test.json', result)
    print(json.dumps({'stage': 'test', 'rows': result['rows']}), flush=True)
    users = evaluate('HW6_EXPERIMENT.collectUsers()')
    save('users.json', users)
    bundle = evaluate('HW6_EXPERIMENT.bundle()')
    save('bundle.json', bundle)
    from export_evidence import export_and_validate
    print(json.dumps(export_and_validate(ROOT), indent=2), flush=True)


def main():
    TEMP.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('action', choices=['start', 'serve', 'reset', 'eval', 'pipeline'])
    parser.add_argument('expression', nargs='?')
    parser.add_argument('--out')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.action == 'serve':
        serve()
    elif args.action == 'reset':
        reset()
    elif args.action == 'start':
        try:
            print(json.dumps(targets(), indent=2))
            return
        except OSError:
            pass
        subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, str(Path(__file__).resolve()), 'serve'],
                         cwd=ROOT, start_new_session=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                         stdout=(TEMP / 'server.log').open('a'), stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        for _ in range(100):
            time.sleep(.2)
            try:
                if targets():
                    print('Started isolated Chrome; application: http://127.0.0.1:8766/index.html')
                    return
            except OSError:
                pass
        raise RuntimeError('Chrome did not start; inspect /tmp/opencode/server.log')
    elif args.action == 'pipeline':
        pipeline()
    else:
        value = evaluate(args.expression)
        if args.out:
            output = Path(args.out)
            if not output.is_absolute():
                output = ROOT / output
            output.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
        print(json.dumps(value.get('summary', value) if isinstance(value, dict) else value,
                         ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# HW6 Step 4A — Final Read-Only Audit

**Main finding:** the graph, PageRank/PPR implementation, dataset continuity, and recorded retrieval calculations are supported by the current source and evidence. However, **the existing HW6 MF row does not satisfy Section 6’s requirement to reuse your corrected HW5 implementation and selected model**.

The HW5 session establishes a corrected model selected at **epoch 19**. HW6 instead trained the supplied, materially different reference model and selected **epoch 1**.

This audit used source inspection, session inspection, hashes, and arithmetic checks against saved outputs. **No application experiments or training were rerun.**

---

## A. Project access results

Both directories are accessible:

- `/home/dastan/Recommender Systems/Week 5`
- `/home/dastan/Recommender Systems/Week 6`

### Files located and inspected

| Material | Result |
|---|---|
| HW5 completed `script.js` and `data.js` | Available |
| HW5 OpenCode session | `Week 5/seikh_abaidullah_a05_session.json` |
| HW6 authoritative `readme.md` | Available; all 11 sections reviewed |
| HW6 implemented graph and recommendation code | Available |
| HW6 student `README.md` | Available |
| HW6 experiment driver, saved measurements, CSVs and verification | Available |
| HW6 saved MF factor arrays | `Week 6/evidence/mf-checkpoint.json` |
| HW6 OpenCode session | Located in **Downloads**, not inside Week 6 |
| Original corrected HW5 model weights | **Not located** |

The HW6 session is:

`/home/dastan/Downloads/hw6-step-1-starter-audit-and-baseline-verification.json`

Despite its “Step 1” filename, its contents include later implementation, verification, and completed experiment records.

Both session exports were preserved. Their hashes remained unchanged during this audit:

```text
HW5 session:
99e4a3d6b70fc17ab24b22d26c436930b872044f0789982c3b1b596ef9a94bc8

HW6 session:
e6243d4e986bfe7c4df06f887dbde6be5f8ad564fdf2c903e32ec0a97172d55f
```

## B. HW5–HW6 dataset continuity

**Status: COMPLETE / PASS.**

The following files are byte-identical between HW5 and HW6:

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `u.data` | `06416e597f82b7342361e41163890c81036900f418ad91315590814211dca490` |
| `u.item` | `553841ebc7de3a0fd0d6b62a204ea30c1e651aacfb2814c7a6584ac52f2c5701` |
| `data.js` | `eb33f8441f652938cce07e7fc7fe1e36f38acd0b296234074ac90d367e2678cd` |

A read-only count and split reconstruction from the existing data agreed with the saved evidence:

| Quantity | Verified value |
|---|---:|
| Users | 943 |
| Catalog movies | 1,682 |
| Ratings | 100,000 |
| Training records | 79,619 |
| Validation records | 9,596 |
| Test records | 10,785 |
| Users excluded during splitting | 0 |
| Duplicate user–movie rating pairs | 0 |
| Training-movie candidates | 1,611 |
| Catalog movies outside the training pool | 71 |
| Distinct positive training edges | 45,602 |
| Zero-degree users | 1: user 685 |
| Zero-degree training movies | 253 |

### Parsing and splitting

`data.js:76–112` parses movie metadata and four-field rating records. Genre parsing correctly uses fields **6–23**, excluding the legacy “unknown” flag.

`data.js:144–184` implements:

- Per-user chronological ordering.
- Ascending movie ID for timestamp ties.
- `floor(0.8 × n)` training records.
- `floor(0.1 × n)` validation records.
- Remaining records assigned to test.

Both projects interpret matrix zero as **unobserved**, not a zero-valued training target. MF training uses observed training records; graph edges use positive training records.

### Leakage assessment

No test-rating contribution to graph construction, popularity, MF fitting, or alpha/checkpoint selection was found in the inspected execution paths.

The loader creates an all-ratings matrix, but the relevant training procedures use the split arrays rather than fitting against that matrix.

The disclosed limitations remain accurate:

- Chronology is per user, not globally time-consistent.
- Timestamps represent ratings, not viewing sessions.
- UTF-8 decoding produces 12 replacement characters in metadata.
- Actual sparsity is approximately **93.69533%**; the starter’s padded display gives **93.71%**.

These limitations do not establish a dataset-continuity failure.

## C. Graph and PageRank/PPR compliance

**Status: COMPLETE / PASS for the implemented and recorded experiments.**

| Requirement | Audit finding |
|---|---|
| Training-only positives, rating ≥4 | Implemented in `graph.js:358–397`; training split supplied by application |
| Bipartite user–movie graph | Only user–movie edges; both propagation directions included |
| Contiguous indexing, no padding | Sorted ID maps; 943 + 1,611 = 2,554 nodes |
| Row normalization | Each positive-degree outgoing row divided by its degree |
| Dangling-node handling | Dangling mass redistributed through the same restart distribution |
| Uniform global PageRank | Uniform restart over all graph nodes |
| User-specific PPR | One-hot restart at the mapped user node |
| Initialization | `p = v` |
| TensorFlow.js core propagation | `tf.matMul` or WASM `tf.sparse.sparseSegmentSum` |
| Convergence | L1 residual below `1e-6`; at most 500 iterations |
| Movie-score extraction | User-node scores excluded |
| Candidate filtering | Training movies only; split-specific previously-rated exclusions |
| Ordering | Descending score, ascending movie ID for ties |
| Tensor management | Per-call cleanup; saved graph/evaluation memory checks support no propagation-tensor accumulation |

Key implementation locations are `graph.js:423–438`, `graph.js:557–696`, and `script.js:1112–1240`.

The authorized adapter corrections are present:

- `script.js:1511` passes the mapped seed index.
- `script.js:1560–1563` rejects unknown raw user IDs rather than treating them as node indices.

### Verification was actually executed

The current `verification.json`, saved setup evidence, and HW6 session contain executed checks—not merely test definitions:

- **12 original checks passed; 0 failed; 0 pending.**
- The session additionally records the independent/integration suite reaching **33 passed, 0 failed** after earlier adapter failures were corrected.

Recorded reference-fixture results include:

| Fixture | Maximum absolute error against specification | Iterations | Ranking |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Uniform restart, α=0.85 | Approximately `1.53e-7` | 28 | C > A > B > D |
| Restart at A, α=0.85 | Approximately `1.14e-7` | 30 | A > C > B > D |

Additional executed checks cover normalization, restart distributions, mass, nonnegativity, stationarity, dangling nodes, orientation, filtering, and indexing.

**Nonconvergence is disclosed correctly:** 27 validation PPR runs at α=0.95 reached the cap. All selected-alpha test walks converged. The specification requires reporting capped runs; it does not require changing the tolerance or repeating them until they converge.

No graph/PPR correction is justified by this audit.

## D. HW5 MF implementation verification

**The corrected HW5 implementation is verified in both current source and recorded runtime evidence.**

The current HW5 `script.js` hash is:

```text
1475668aec8c1b008b8b9c6c0b3302f16e9c7bca326e32ea5a0cd7a11e8d51e1
```

It matches the corrected Step 2C hash recorded in the HW5 session.

### Implementation comparison

| Property | Corrected HW5 | Current HW6 reference |
|---|---|---|
| Basic score | Training mean + user/item dot product | Same basic formula |
| Rating prediction / validation RMSE | Predictions clamped to `[1,5]` | No equivalent prediction clamp |
| Recommendation scores | Raw, unclamped mean-plus-dot | Raw, unclamped mean-plus-dot |
| Latent factors | 16 | 16 |
| Initialization | Unseeded `tf.randomNormal`, SD 0.05 | Seeded Mulberry32/Box–Muller, SD 0.05 |
| Optimizer | Adam | Adam |
| Learning rate | 0.01 in recorded corrected run | 0.01 |
| Batch size | **64** | **512** |
| Regularization coefficient | 0.05 | 0.05 |
| Regularization formulation | **Batch-average squared norms of gathered rows** | **Unnormalized sum over both complete factor matrices per batch** |
| Batch order | Existing ordered training records | Seeded shuffle each epoch |
| Epochs | **20** | **30** |
| Training records | Same 79,619 training records | Same 79,619 training records |
| Checkpoint criterion | Minimum validation RMSE, earliest tie | Minimum validation RMSE, earliest tie |
| Restoration | Copies best factor tensors back | Assigns saved best factor arrays |
| Recorded selected epoch | **19** | **1** |

The corrected HW5 penalty is at `Week 5/script.js:513`:

```js
u.square().sum(1).add(i.square().sum(1)).mean().mul(reg)
```

The HW6 penalty at `Week 6/script.js:953` is materially different:

```js
userFactors.square().sum()
  .add(itemFactors.square().sum())
  .mul(MF_CONFIG.reg)
```

### HW5 session evidence

The session contains the diagnosis, controlled alternatives, exact correction, and actual corrected full-run tool output.

The corrected full run recorded:

- 20 epochs, 16 factors, Adam, LR 0.01, regularization 0.05, batch size 64.
- **Selected epoch: 19.**
- Selected validation RMSE: **1.0714447826339824**.
- Active restored validation RMSE: **1.0714447826339824**.
- Test RMSE: **1.1164852682970523**.
- Original-protocol Recall@10: **0.005005283353211099**.
- **11 passed / 0 failed / 0 pending**.
- Non-degenerate recommendation scores.

The seeds 205 and 206 mentioned in that session belong to the controlled diagnostic initialization. **They are not evidence of the seed used for the final unseeded corrected model.**

## E. Existing HW6 MF comparison

**Status: REQUIRED FIX / MF continuity FAIL.**

The existing HW6 MF experiment is genuine and internally supported, but it evaluates the **supplied HW6 reference**, not the corrected previous recommender.

Its saved results are:

- Selected epoch: **1**.
- Validation RMSE: **1.1829944264078285**.
- Test Recall@10: **0.021137488852036153**.
- Every audited test candidate score: **3.5806026458740234**.
- Consequently, recommendation ordering is determined by exclusions and ascending-ID ties.

This resembles the **discarded pre-correction behavior** documented in HW5 Step 2B. Similar metrics do not establish identical weights or model reuse.

The student README already discloses this limitation honestly. However:

> Disclosure satisfies the obligation to identify incomplete work; it does not, by itself, satisfy Section 6’s separate requirement to reuse the previous implementation and selected model.

The existing MF result should remain preserved as a **supplied-reference diagnostic**, not be relabeled as corrected HW5 MF.

## F. Original HW5 checkpoint availability

**Original selected-model metadata is available. Original selected weights were not found.**

The search covered:

- The Recommender Systems project tree.
- Downloads, Documents, and Desktop using model/checkpoint/weight-related names and common weight formats.
- Relevant `/tmp/opencode` artifacts.
- Embedded HW5 session outputs and the recorded full-run evidence-generation code.

The recorded HW5 full-run script reads factor values to calculate norms and independent RMSEs, but its returned evidence contains **statistics and selected recommendation lists**, not the complete factor arrays.

No saved full HW5 user/item factor matrices or corresponding model serialization were located.

### What is recoverable?

| Artifact | Availability |
|---|---|
| Corrected implementation | Available |
| Hyperparameters and training protocol | Available |
| Selected epoch 19 and metrics | Available |
| Training history | Available in session |
| Selected recommendation examples | Available in session |
| Original selected factor arrays | **Unavailable in inspected artifacts** |

The current `evidence/mf-checkpoint.json` contains actual arrays of shapes **944×16** and **1,683×16**, but they belong to **HW6’s reference epoch-1 model**. Their fingerprints match the saved HW6 experiment.

They cannot be relabeled as HW5 weights.

**Direct evaluation of the original corrected model is therefore not currently possible from the located artifacts.** Metrics, norms, and Top-10 examples are insufficient to reconstruct all factors, particularly with unseeded initialization.

If an original backup is later supplied, the least invasive route is to load those arrays without training, verify their shapes/global mean and restored validation result, and evaluate their raw scores under HW6’s candidate and cohort rules.

## G. Shared evaluation protocol verification

**The recorded comparison follows the HW6 retrieval protocol. Its separate failure is the identity of the MF model.**

### Verified controls

- Same 1,611 training-movie candidates.
- Same **861 test user IDs**, not merely the same count.
- Training presence, positive training edge, and eligible relevance requirements.
- Supplied MF can score all required candidates.
- Validation excludes training-rated movies.
- Test excludes training- and validation-rated movies.
- Exclusion ignores the historical rating value.
- Relevance threshold is ≥4.
- Recall is a macro mean of per-user recall.
- Explicit exclusions are consistent with raw data.
- No test-based selection found in the recorded experiment sequence.

| Exclusion | Validation | Test |
|---|---:|---:|
| Users without eligible relevance | 97 | 82 |
| Users without positive training edges | 1 | 1 |
| Excluded user union | 97 | 82 |
| Relevant records outside candidate pool | 4 | 13 |

The user exclusions overlap; they must not be added as independent counts.

### Alpha selection

| Alpha | Validation Recall@10 | Nonconverged users |
|---|---:|---:|
| **0.50** | **0.1144831591** | 0 |
| 0.70 | 0.1047969508 | 0 |
| 0.85 | 0.0900207716 | 0 |
| 0.95 | 0.0737503039 | 27 |

Selection uses validation only, with smaller-alpha tie-breaking. Both primary graph methods use **0.50**.

The saved timestamps place selection before MF training and final test evaluation. The ordered experiment driver enforces that sequence. The starter’s combined recall button does not independently enforce it, but the documented driver used for the saved results does.

### Controlled demonstrations

The fixed users are **1 and 2**:

| Setting | User | Alpha | Mean popularity | Overlap with baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 1 | 0.85 | 245.5 | 10 |
| Change user/seed | 2 | 0.85 | 254.9 | 0 |
| Change alpha | 1 | 0.50 | 228.4 | 7 |

These match Section 6.2. Changing user also applies that user’s exclusions; the documentation acknowledges this.

### Why HW5 Recall@10 cannot be copied into HW6

Corrected HW5 `recommendTopK()` ranks eligible movies from the **whole metadata catalog**. Its `recallAtK()` restricts relevant-item eligibility to training movies but consumes the catalog-wide Top-10.

HW6 instead restricts **ranking itself** to training movies.

HW6 also explicitly requires positive training edges and common MF scoreability. The saved datasets happen to yield the same 861 test-user count, but equal counts do not make the candidate protocols equivalent.

Therefore, HW5’s **0.005005283353211099** is historical evidence, **not a valid replacement HW6 MF row** without reevaluation.

## H. Existing experiment and evidence integrity

**Status: PASS for the measurements actually represented.**

I performed read-only consistency checks against saved artifacts:

- All **9 source/data hashes** recorded by the experiment match current files.
- The additional source-integrity manifest also matches.
- All **6,828 saved user/method/alpha lists** agree with raw-data candidate membership, exclusions, relevance, hits, ordering, and popularity.
- Macro recall and mean popularity agree with their saved summaries.
- All **8 `results.csv` rows** agree with the underlying audits.
- All **110 recommendation rows** agree with saved lists, titles, genres, scores, and popularity.
- Saved HW6 factor arrays have the expected dimensions and finite values.
- Their reconstructed float32 hashes match the frozen-model fingerprints.
- Before/after-test fingerprints agree.

The existing test table is supported:

| Method | Recall@10 |
|---|---:|
| Popularity | 0.0760229134 |
| Global PageRank | 0.0796932415 |
| PPR | 0.1121885322 |
| **Supplied HW6 MF reference** | 0.0211374889 |

The HW6 session contains corresponding execution outputs. It also retains earlier failures and subsequent corrections.

**Evidence integrity and assignment compliance are different:** this table is supported as a comparison with the supplied reference, but it is not yet the required comparison with corrected HW5 MF.

## I. Missing HW6 requirements

### Report evidence availability

| Section 8 requirement | Availability |
|---|---|
| Shared-cohort results | Available for current four implementations |
| Required previous-MF result under HW6 protocol | **Missing** |
| Two-user Top-10 lists, titles, genres | Available |
| Training histories and preference examples | Available |
| Per-item and mean training popularity | Available |
| Within-method overlap | Available |
| Seed-change and alpha-change demonstrations | Available |
| Model and evaluation limitations | Available |
| Final answer to the single business question | Not yet written |
| One proposed online experiment | Not yet written |
| Primary outcome, guardrail, user-level assignment | Not yet written |

The available evidence supports discussion of the implemented graph methods and the reference-model failure. **It is insufficient for an assignment-compliant decision about keeping or replacing the corrected previous MF model.**

The final report is intentionally outside this audit. Its absence is not a violation of the Step 4A instructions.

## J. Required fixes versus optional improvements

| Classification | Issue |
|---|---|
| **REQUIRED FIX** | Resolve Section 6 MF continuity: the current reference is not the corrected HW5 implementation or selected model |
| **REQUIRED FIX** | Once the MF route is resolved, supply its HW6-protocol metrics and associated two-user evidence; do not substitute old HW5 recall |
| **REQUIRED FIX — reporting stage** | Answer exactly the specified business question and include the required online intervention, primary outcome, guardrail, and contamination-resistant user assignment |
| **VERIFICATION NEEDED** | Instructor acceptance of a newly trained reproduction if original weights remain unavailable |
| **VERIFICATION NEEDED** | Current grading guide, submission location, deadline, and AI-export requirement |
| **VERIFICATION NEEDED** | Bibliographic verification before including citations in the final report |
| **VERIFICATION NEEDED** | Final packaging of the unmodified HW6 session export, currently in Downloads |
| **OPTIONAL IMPROVEMENT** | Add model provenance directly to CSV fields rather than relying on the README |
| **OPTIONAL IMPROVEMENT** | Correct stale adapter JSDoc that still describes raw-ID passing despite the fixed node-index call |
| **COMPLETE** | Dataset continuity, graph/PPR implementation, alpha selection, graph-method results, controlled demonstrations, and current evidence exports |

Additional alpha tuning, changing the iteration cap, multi-seed comparisons, and retraining to improve metrics are **not necessary corrections identified by this audit**.

## K. Recommended minimum correction

### Option 1 — Recover the original model

This is the least invasive and closest literal compliance:

1. Obtain the actual corrected HW5 epoch-19 factor arrays from a genuine backup.
2. Load and verify them.
3. Evaluate them under the existing HW6 protocol.

**Currently blocked by missing weights.**

### Option 2 — Transparent disclosure only

Preserve the current table and disclose unavailable HW5 weights and the substituted model.

This is honest, but **does not automatically fulfill the previous-model reuse requirement**. It is a compliant substitution only if the instructor explicitly accepts it.

### Option 3 — Corrected-HW5 reproduction

If no original weights can be provided, the minimum technically meaningful correction is a **new, explicitly labeled reproduction of the corrected HW5 implementation**, subject to authorization and acceptance of the missing-original-model limitation.

It should preserve the recorded settings and behavior:

- 16 factors.
- 20 epochs.
- Adam, LR 0.01.
- Batch size 64.
- Batch-row regularization coefficient 0.05.
- Original training order.
- Original clamped validation-RMSE definition.
- Validation-selected checkpoint with restoration.
- Original raw recommendation-score formula.

A newly selected epoch need not be 19. **Do not force epoch 19 or claim exact reproduction of its weights.**

This is justified by implementation continuity, **not by a desire for higher recall**. It restores the corrected implementation comparison but cannot retroactively recover the original selected model.

**Recommendation:** retain all completed evidence, first seek the original checkpoint or confirmation that none exists, then resolve whether a clearly labeled corrected-HW5 reproduction is accepted.

## L. Proposed next implementation step, only if needed

A narrowly scoped MF-continuity step is needed if proceeding toward full compliance.

After choosing the recovery/reproduction route:

1. Add an isolated HW5-compatible MF integration in HW6.
2. Preserve the current reference model, weights, results, and session exports.
3. Verify raw-ID factor mapping, scoreability, prediction/ranking definitions, and checkpoint restoration.
4. Evaluate only the recovered/reproduced MF under the existing HW6 protocol.
5. Retain α=0.50 and users 1/2.
6. Produce versioned MF metrics, lists, popularity, overlaps, and provenance.
7. Reuse the completed graph-method results if the verified shared cohort is unchanged.

No PageRank/PPR implementation change or alpha-sweep repetition is presently justified.

**This next step has not been implemented.**

## M. Final submission readiness

| Deliverable | Status |
|---|---|
| JavaScript application and source | Present |
| Student README | Present; versions, run instructions, and limitations documented |
| `verification.json` | Present and supported |
| `results.csv` | Present; required corrected-HW5 MF comparison unresolved |
| `recommendations.csv` | Present; same MF qualification |
| MF checkpoint evidence | Present for HW6 reference; original HW5 weights unavailable |
| HW5 original session export | Present |
| HW6 original session export | Present in Downloads; final packaging still needed |
| `report.pdf` | Not generated; appropriately deferred during this audit |
| Instructor confirmations | Unverified |

**The project is ready for a narrowly scoped MF-continuity resolution, not final submission.** The completed graph work should be preserved.

---

## **AUDIT SUMMARY**

**HW5 access: PASS**

**HW6 access: PASS**

**Graph/PPR compliance: PASS** — capped α=0.95 runs are disclosed.

**Dataset continuity: PASS**

**MF continuity: FAIL** — the current HW6 reference is not the corrected HW5 implementation or original selected model.

**Shared evaluation: PASS** — for the recorded implementations; the MF-identity failure remains separate.

**Evidence integrity: PASS** — saved outputs, arithmetic, source hashes, checkpoint hashes, and session records agree.

**Submission readiness: FAIL** — mandatory MF continuity is unresolved; final reporting and submission confirmations remain pending.

**Required fixes:**
- Resolve previous-MF reuse or obtain explicit acceptance of a disclosed substitute.
- Supply the appropriate MF results under the HW6 protocol.
- Complete the single business analysis and required online-experiment proposal during the report step.

**Optional improvements:**
- Add explicit model provenance to CSV fields.
- Correct stale adapter documentation.

**Files modified: NO**

**Experiments rerun: NO**

**Existing evidence overwritten: NO**

**Recommended next action:** resolve original HW5 checkpoint availability and acceptance of a corrected-HW5 reproduction, then authorize only the necessary MF integration/evaluation step. **Stop here; no corrections or final report have been generated.**

249: /**
250:  * Root-mean-square error of the current model over a split.
251:  *
252:  * Provided so that `trainMF` and the test harness share one implementation.
253:  *
254:  * When `model` holds TF.js variables this builds the index tensors ONCE, uses
255:  * `tf.gather` + element-wise multiply to score every rating in a single batch,
256:  * and clamps to `[1, 5]` — the same contract as `predictRating`, but fast
257:  * enough to call every epoch. Out-of-range ids fall back to `globalMean`, and
258:  * the whole computation runs inside `tf.tidy` so the intermediate tensors are
259:  * released automatically.
260:  *
261:  * When no TF.js model is available it falls back to the scalar
262:  * `predictRating` loop. That path returns `NaN` instead of throwing while
263:  * `predictRating` is still a `TODO(hw5)` stub, so the helper never crashes the
264:  * page or the harness.
265:  *
266:  * @param {Rating[]} split
267:  * @returns {number} `0` for an empty split; `NaN` if the scalar path throws.
268:  */
269: function computeRMSEFor(split) {
270:   if (!split || split.length === 0) return 0;
271: 
272:   if (isTfModel(model)) {
273:     return tf.tidy(() => {
274:       const n = split.length;
275:       const uRows = model.userFactors.shape[0];
276:       const iRows = model.itemFactors.shape[0];
277:       const userIds = new Int32Array(n);
278:       const movieIds = new Int32Array(n);
279:       const actual = new Float32Array(n);
280:       const valid = new Float32Array(n);
281: 
282:       for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
283:         const r = split[k];
284:         userIds[k] = r.userId;
285:         movieIds[k] = r.movieId;
286:         actual[k] = r.rating;
287:         const uOk = r.userId >= 0 && r.userId < uRows;
288:         const iOk = r.movieId >= 0 && r.movieId < iRows;
289:         valid[k] = uOk && iOk ? 1 : 0;
290:       }
291: 
292:       const uIdx = tf.clipByValue(tf.tensor1d(userIds, "int32"), 0, Math.max(0, uRows - 1));
293:       const iIdx = tf.clipByValue(tf.tensor1d(movieIds, "int32"), 0, Math.max(0, iRows - 1));
294:       const u = tf.gather(model.userFactors, uIdx);
295:       const i = tf.gather(model.itemFactors, iIdx);
296:       const dot = tf.sum(tf.mul(u, i), 1);
297:       const mask = tf.tensor1d(valid, "float32");
298:       const pred = tf.clipByValue(dot.mul(mask).add(model.globalMean), 1, 5);
299:       const diff = pred.sub(tf.tensor1d(actual, "float32"));
300:       return Math.sqrt(tf.mean(diff.square()).dataSync()[0]);
301:     });
302:   }
303: 
304:   let sum = 0;
305:   try {
306:     for (const r of split) {
307:       const diff = predictRating(r.userId, r.movieId) - r.rating;
308:       sum += diff * diff;
309:     }
310:   } catch (error) {
311:     return Number.NaN;
312:   }
313:   return Math.sqrt(sum / split.length);
314: }
315:

317:  * Baseline RMSE: predict the training-set mean rating for every pair and
318:  * measure the error on `split`. This is the number your factorization must beat.
319:  *
320:  * @param {Rating[]} split
321:  * @returns {number} `0` for an empty split (never divides by zero).
322:  */
323: function computeBaselineRMSE(split) {
324:   if (!split || split.length === 0) return 0;
325:   const mean = trainSet.length
326:     ? trainSet.reduce((acc, r) => acc + r.rating, 0) / trainSet.length
327:     : 0;
328:   let sum = 0;
329:   for (const r of split) {
330:     const diff = mean - r.rating;
331:     sum += diff * diff;
332:   }
333:   return Math.sqrt(sum / split.length);
334: }

344:  * Predict the rating a user would give a movie (scalar).

346:  * TODO(hw5): implement the prediction with TensorFlow.js. The model stores the
347:  * factors as two dense `tf.Variable`s:
348:  *   - `model.userFactors` shape `[numUsers + 1, F]`, row index = `userId`
349:  *   - `model.itemFactors` shape `[maxMovieId + 1, F]`, row index = `movieId`

351:  * Suggested TF.js path (wrap it in `tf.tidy` and pull out a JS number):

353:  * const f = model.userFactors.shape[1];
354:  * return tf.tidy(() => {
355:  *   const u = model.userFactors.slice([userId, 0], [1, f]); // [1, F]
356:  *   const i = model.itemFactors.slice([movieId, 0], [1, f]); // [1, F]
357:  *   const dot = u.mul(i).sum().dataSync()[0];                // scalar
358:  *   return clamp(model.globalMean + dot, 1, 5);
359:  * });
360:  * ```
361:  * `dataSync()` copies the value to the CPU as a plain number, which survives
362:  * `tf.tidy` (the tensors do not). Keep this function scalar: `computeRMSEFor`
363:  * uses its own batched tensor path, and the harness calls it once per pair.
364:  *
365:  * Contract:
366:  *  - Return `model.globalMean` when the user or movie row is out of range
367:  *    (an id that has no allocated factor row). Never throw for an unknown id.
368:  *  - Return `0` when the model is not initialized (`model === null`) so callers
369:  *    can guard cheaply.
370:  *  - The result is clamped to `[1, 5]`.
371:  *
372:  * @param {number} userId
373:  * @param {number} movieId
374:  * @returns {number} predicted rating in `[1, 5]`
375:  */
376: function predictRating(userId, movieId) {
377:   if (model === null) return 0;
378:   if (
379:     !Number.isInteger(userId) || userId < 0 || userId >= model.userFactors.shape[0] ||
380:     !Number.isInteger(movieId) || movieId < 0 || movieId >= model.itemFactors.shape[0]
381:   ) return model.globalMean;
382: 
383:   return tf.tidy(() => {
384:     const f = model.userFactors.shape[1];
385:     const u = model.userFactors.slice([userId, 0], [1, f]);
386:     const i = model.itemFactors.slice([movieId, 0], [1, f]);
387:     return clamp(model.globalMean + u.mul(i).sum().dataSync()[0], 1, 5);
388:   });

391: /**

393:  *
394:  * TODO(hw5): compute `globalMean` as the mean rating over `train`
395:  * (`0` for an empty training set), then create the two dense variables:
396:  * ```js
397:  * const maxMovieId = movies.reduce((m, x) => Math.max(m, x.id), 0);
398:  * model = {
399:  *   userFactors: tf.variable(tf.randomNormal([numUsers + 1, numFactors], 0, 0.05)),
400:  *   itemFactors: tf.variable(tf.randomNormal([maxMovieId + 1, numFactors], 0, 0.05)),
401:  *   globalMean,

404:  * `tf.randomNormal(shape, mean, std)` draws small values — use a small std
405:  * (e.g. `0.05`) so training starts near the global mean. `tf.variable` wraps a
406:  * tensor so the optimizer can update it in place. Store the result on the
407:  * module-level `model` object and return it.
408:  *
409:  * Contract:
410:  *  - `numFactors` defaults to the module-level `NUM_FACTORS`.
411:  *  - If a previous `model` exists, dispose its variables (`tf.dispose`) before
412:  *    replacing it so repeated "Train" clicks do not leak GPU memory.

415:  * @param {Rating[]} train
416:  * @param {number} [numFactors=NUM_FACTORS]

472:  *  - Append one `HistoryRow` per epoch to the module-level `trainingHistory`
473:  *    and return it: `{ epoch, trainRMSE: computeRMSEFor(train),
474:  *    valRMSE: computeRMSEFor(val) }`. `epoch` is 1-based.

485:   if (train.length === 0) return trainingHistory;
486: 
487:   const { epochs, lr, reg } = opts;
488:   const batchSize = Math.max(1, Math.floor(opts.batchSize));
489:   const optimizer = tf.train.adam(lr);
490:   const userIds = Int32Array.from(train, (r) => r.userId);
491:   const itemIds = Int32Array.from(train, (r) => r.movieId);
492:   const targets = Float32Array.from(train, (r) => r.rating);
493:   let bestRow = null;
494:   let bestUsers = null;
495:   let bestItems = null;
496: 
497:   try {
498:     for (let epoch = 1; epoch <= epochs; epoch++) {
499:       for (let start = 0; start < train.length; start += batchSize) {
500:         const end = Math.min(start + batchSize, train.length);
501:         tf.tidy(() => {
502:           const userIdx = tf.tensor1d(userIds.subarray(start, end), "int32");
503:           const itemIdx = tf.tensor1d(itemIds.subarray(start, end), "int32");
504:           const actual = tf.tensor1d(targets.subarray(start, end));
505:           // returnCost=false returns no loss tensor; tidy releases intermediates.
506:           optimizer.minimize(() => {
507:             const u = tf.gather(model.userFactors, userIdx);
508:             const i = tf.gather(model.itemFactors, itemIdx);
509:             const pred = tf.sum(u.mul(i), 1).add(model.globalMean);
510:             const mse = tf.losses.meanSquaredError(actual, pred);
511:             // Average squared row norms over this batch, matching the MSE scale.
512:             // Penalize participating rows, not every factor at every batch update.
513:             const l2 = u.square().sum(1).add(i.square().sum(1)).mean().mul(reg);
514:             return mse.add(l2);
515:           }, false, [model.userFactors, model.itemFactors]);
516:         });
517:       }
518: 
519:       const row = {
520:         epoch,
521:         trainRMSE: computeRMSEFor(train),
522:         valRMSE: computeRMSEFor(val),
523:       };
524:       trainingHistory.push(row);
525:       // Epochs are ascending: strict improvement preserves the earliest tie.
526:       if (bestRow === null || row.valRMSE < bestRow.valRMSE) {

549:  * entry with the EARLIEST `epoch` (do not simply take the last minimum). This
550:  * one is plain JavaScript — no TF.js needed.
551:  *
552:  * Contract:
553:  *  - Return `null` for an empty or missing history.
554:  *  - Do not mutate the input array.
555:  *
556:  * @param {HistoryRow[]} history
557:  * @returns {HistoryRow|null}
558:  */
559: function selectBestCheckpoint(history) {
560:   if (!history || history.length === 0) return null;
561:   let best = history[0];
562:   for (const row of history) {
563:     if (
564:       row.valRMSE < best.valRMSE ||
565:       (row.valRMSE === best.valRMSE && row.epoch < best.epoch)
566:     ) best = row;
567:   }
568:   return best;
569: }
570: 
571: /**
572:  * Recommend the top-K movies for a user.
573:  *
574:  * TODO(hw5): score every candidate movie and return the K highest-scoring
575:  * movies the user has NOT already rated in `trainSet` or `valSet`. Test-set
576:  * ratings are allowed as candidates. **Prefer the tensor path**:
577:  * ```js
578:  * const userRow = model.userFactors.slice([userId, 0], [1, F]); // [1, F]
579:  * const scores = model.itemFactors.matMul(userRow, false, true)  // [rows, 1]
580:  *   .squeeze().add(model.globalMean);                            // [rows]
581:  * // mask excluded ids to a large negative value, then:
582:  * const { values, indices } = tf.topk(maskedScores, Math.min(K, rows));
583:  * ```
584:  * Because `itemFactors` is indexed by raw `movieId`, the `tf.topk` indices ARE
585:  * the movie ids — no reverse mapping needed. Excluded rows must be masked (for
586:  * example multiply by a 0/1 mask and add `(1 - mask) * -1e9`); re-apply the
587:  * same mask when mapping results back so masked ids are dropped.
588:  *
589:  * Contract:
590:  *  - Return `[{ movieId, title, score }, ...]` sorted by descending `score`,
591:  *    truncated to `K` (fewer if not enough candidates).
592:  *  - Exclude any movie id that is absent from the global `movies` list, and any
593:  *    id the user rated in `trainSet` or `valSet`.
594:  *  - Return `[]` when the model is not initialized, when `K <= 0`, or when the
595:  *    user has no eligible candidates — never throw.
596:  *  - `title` comes from `movieTitle(movieId)`.
597:  *
598:  * @param {number} userId
599:  * @param {number} [K=10]
600:  * @returns {Array<{movieId: number, title: string, score: number}>}
601:  */
602: function recommendTopK(userId, K = 10) {
603:   if (!model || !(K > 0)) return [];
604:   if (!Number.isInteger(userId) || userId < 0 || userId >= model.userFactors.shape[0]) {
605:     return [];
606:   }
607:   const excluded = new Set();
608:   for (const r of trainSet) if (r.userId === userId) excluded.add(r.movieId);
609:   for (const r of valSet) if (r.userId === userId) excluded.add(r.movieId);
610:   const rows = model.itemFactors.shape[0];
611:   const eligible = new Set(movies
612:     .map((movie) => movie.id)
613:     .filter((id) => Number.isInteger(id) && id >= 0 && id < rows && !excluded.has(id)));
614:   const count = Math.min(Math.floor(K), eligible.size);
615:   if (count <= 0) return [];
616: 
617:   return tf.tidy(() => {
618:     const userRow = model.userFactors.slice([userId, 0], [1, model.userFactors.shape[1]]);
619:     // Rank raw mean-plus-dot scores, as in the supplied recommendation example.
620:     const scores = model.itemFactors.matMul(userRow, false, true)
621:       .reshape([rows]).add(model.globalMean);
622:     const mask = new Uint8Array(rows);
623:     for (const id of eligible) mask[id] = 1;
624:     const masked = tf.where(tf.tensor1d(mask, "bool"), scores, tf.fill([rows], -Infinity));
625:     const { values, indices } = tf.topk(masked, count, true);
626:     const ids = indices.dataSync();
627:     const rankedScores = values.dataSync();
628:     return Array.from(ids, (movieId, index) => ({
629:       movieId,
630:       title: movieTitle(movieId),
631:       score: rankedScores[index],
632:     })).filter((r) => eligible.has(r.movieId));
633:   });
634: }
635: 
636: /**
637:  * Compute Recall@K for the current model.
638:  *
639:  * TODO(hw5): retrieval evaluation built on `recommendTopK`.
640:  *   - relevant = test ratings with `rating >= 4.0`.
641:  *   - Candidate items = the set of movie ids that appear anywhere in `trainSet`
642:  *     (a global candidate pool, NOT just the user's own training items).
643:  *   - For every user with at least one relevant test movie among the
644:  *     candidates, take `recommendTopK(userId, K)` and count how many of that
645:  *     user's relevant candidate movies appear in it.
646:  *
647:  * Contract:
648:  *  - Return
649:  *    `{ overallRecall, perUser, excluded }` where:
650:  *      `overallRecall` = mean over reported users of `hit / relevant`
651:  *        (`0` when there are no reported users — never divide by zero);
652:  *      `perUser` = `[{ userId, relevant, hit }, ...]` (reported users only);
653:  *      `excluded` = `{ unseenIds, usersWithoutRelevant }`.
654:  *  - `unseenIds` = distinct relevant test movie ids that are NOT present in
655:  *    `trainSet` (they can never be recommended from a training-only pool).
656:  *  - `usersWithoutRelevant` = distinct users that appear in `testSet` but have
657:  *    no relevant test movie among the candidates.
658:  *  - Report exclusions explicitly so the recall number is interpretable.
659:  *
660:  * @param {number} [K=10]
661:  * @returns {{overallRecall: number, perUser: Array<{userId: number, relevant: number, hit: number}>, excluded: {unseenIds: number[], usersWithoutRelevant: number[]}}}
662:  */
663: function recallAtK(K = 10) {
664:   const candidates = new Set(trainSet.map((r) => r.movieId));
665:   const relevantByUser = new Map();
666:   const unseenIds = new Set();
667:   for (const r of testSet) {
668:     if (!relevantByUser.has(r.userId)) relevantByUser.set(r.userId, new Set());
669:     if (r.rating >= 4.0) {
670:       if (candidates.has(r.movieId)) relevantByUser.get(r.userId).add(r.movieId);
671:       else unseenIds.add(r.movieId);
672:     }
673:   }
674: 
675:   const perUser = [];
676:   const usersWithoutRelevant = [];
677:   let totalRecall = 0;
678:   for (const [userId, relevantIds] of relevantByUser) {
679:     if (relevantIds.size === 0) {
680:       usersWithoutRelevant.push(userId);
681:       continue;
682:     }
683:     // Training membership defines relevant eligibility; ranking uses the catalog
684:     // Top-K exactly as returned by the recommender (the stub's literal procedure).
685:     const recommendations = recommendTopK(userId, K);
686:     const hit = recommendations.reduce((sum, r) => sum + Number(relevantIds.has(r.movieId)), 0);
687:     perUser.push({ userId, relevant: relevantIds.size, hit });
688:     totalRecall += hit / relevantIds.size;
689:   }
690: 
691:   return {
692:     overallRecall: perUser.length ? totalRecall / perUser.length : 0,
693:     perUser,
694:     excluded: {
695:       unseenIds: Array.from(unseenIds).sort((a, b) => a - b),
696:       usersWithoutRelevant: usersWithoutRelevant.sort((a, b) => a - b),
697:     },
698:   };
699: }

 *
 * Provided so that `trainMF` and the test harness share one implementation.
